The goals of the program are to improve balance, gait, coordination, reaction time, strength, posture, vocal projection, and confidence — all areas commonly affected by Parkinson’s.

Classes are currently offered Mondays and Thursdays from 1:30-2:30pm at Action & Reaction MMA gym.

A medical clearance form must be completed and signed by a physician prior to enrollment. Please contact us at (416) 386-0384 or boxing@balancephysiotherapy.com to obtain this form

Classes are also led by Tracy Tan who is an experienced physiotherapist working with clients with PD. For seniors living in remote and rural communities without easy access to a community class, an online version of our program will be available on YouTube by Spring 2024.

listings.description:
Assessment services include psychodiagnostic and mental health assessments, neuropsychological and cognitive assessments, adult neurodiversity assessments for ADHD and autism, concussion and neurological concerns, learning and disability assessments, psychoeducational assessments, trauma and PTSD, and gender-affirming surgical-readiness second-assessor services. Assessments may help clarify diagnosis, cognitive functioning, treatment needs, accommodations, and practical recommendations for daily life, work, or education.

Psychotherapy services are tailored to each client’s needs, circumstances, and interpersonal style. Areas of support include anxiety and stress, depression and grief, trauma and PTSD, OCD symptoms, relationship concerns, neurodiversity, sexuality and gender, workplace stress, burnout, emotion regulation, self-esteem, and general mental health concerns.
Treatment may incorporate evidence-based approaches including Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT), Dialectical Behaviour Therapy (DBT), Emotion-Focused Therapy (EFT), Internal Family Systems-informed approaches, psychodynamic therapy, and mindfulness-based interventions. Care is collaborative and considers biological, psychological, interpersonal, and social factors when developing treatment recommendations and goals.
listings.expertise: I am a doctoral-level neuropsychologist with specialized training in brain-behaviour relationships, having completed a pre-doctoral internship in neuropsychology and holding registration in Clinical Neuropsychology with the College of Psychologists and Behavioural Analysts of Ontario (CPBAO). My experience working with Parkinson's disease encompasses a thorough understanding of its clinical presentation, motor features, and neurocognitive sequelae, including mild cognitive impairment, Lewy body dementia, and Parkinson's disease dementia. I am skilled in administering and interpreting standardized neuropsychological test batteries tailored to PD, carefully accounting for variables such as bradykinesia, tremor, fatigue, dopaminergic medication timing (on versus off states), and age-related normative data, and I can differentiate PD-related cognitive changes from other etiologies including Alzheimer's dementia, vascular cognitive impairment, depression, medication effects, and reversible causes. In my practice I provide psychoeducation, cognitive rehabilitation strategies, and behavioural interventions to address mood, anxiety, sleep disturbances, impulse control disorders related to dopamine agonists, and caregiver support. I collaborate closely with neurologists, movement disorder specialists, geriatricians, occupational therapists, and speech-language pathologists to inform treatment planning, medication management decisions, and functional capacity assessments, and I maintain my expertise through ongoing engagement with PD-focused research, continuing professional development on evolving pharmacological and surgical treatments such as DBS candidacy, and familiarity with current diagnostic criteria.

Speech-language pathology services for adults focus on maintaining and improving communication, voice, speech clarity, and swallowing safety. Services may include assessment and treatment of reduced vocal loudness, soft or breathy voice, imprecise articulation, rapid speech, changes in facial expression, cognitive-communication difficulties, and swallowing concerns.

Intervention is individualized and may involve voice-strengthening exercises, strategies to improve speech intelligibility, breath support, pacing, communication-partner training, and education for clients and families. Swallowing assessment and therapy may also be provided to support safer eating and drinking, reduce the risk of aspiration, and promote continued participation in daily activities. Treatment emphasizes practical strategies that help individuals communicate confidently and maintain independence throughout the progression of Parkinson's disease.

listings.expertise:
I have experience supporting people living with Parkinson's disease through both group and one-on-one Yoga Therapy sessions. As a Certified Yoga Therapist (C-IAYT), I adapt each practice to the individual's symptoms, abilities, and goals, focusing on improving balance, mobility, strength, flexibility, posture, breathing, and confidence in movement. My approach is grounded in best practices and is compassionate and person-centered, helping individuals move with greater ease, maintain independence, and enhance their quality of life.

In addition to my professional experience, Parkinson's disease is deeply personal to me. My father lived with Parkinson's disease, and accompanying him throughout his journey gave me a meaningful understanding of the daily challenges faced by individuals and their families. His journey continues to inspire my commitment to providing compassionate, individualized care that supports not only physical well-being but also confidence, resilience, and connection.

PWR!Moves for Parkinson’s Level 1: This progressive exercise class will focus on total body exercises that promote flexibility, strength and power. The class will assist participants in maintaining and improving motor skills that are used in everyday activities that have been affected by the progression of Parkinson’s disease. A series of rhythmical exercises are performed lying down on the floor, on all fours, seated and standing.
Note that participants should be at the following fitness level:
Can get up and down the floor alone with or without a chair
Have not had two or more falls in the past 6 months
Have not experienced dizziness when transitioning from lying down to standing or sitting
Can participate in light to moderate cardiovascular intensity

NeuroFit is an 8-week exercise program for adults living with neurological conditions. Led by a Clinical Exercise Physiologist, participants attend two supervised classes per week to improve strength, balance, mobility, endurance, and confidence through safe exercise. An initial Physiotherapy Assessment ensures individualized programming.

Suitable for individuals with Parkinson's disease, Multiple Sclerosis, Stroke, Guillane-Barr© syndrome, Huntington's Disease and other neurological conditions.

To help ensure this program is safe and effective, participants must meet the following participation guidelines:
1. Have a 1:1 Physiotherapy intake appointment at the Wellness Institute to evaluate abilities and limitations.
2. Be able to walk independently, with or without a walking aide, or be accompanied by an attendant.
3. Have the physical ability to actively participate in the exercise session for 45 minutes.
4. Be able to pay attention, follow instructions and mimic exercises. They must be aware of their safe bounds of ability.
5. Be able to manage their own bladder function.
6. Have completed a rehabilitation program after a stroke.
listings.expertise: As a certified medical fitness facility, we have extensive experience supporting individuals with Parkinson's disease and other neurological conditions. We use exercise interventions including core strengthening, gait training and high repetition, load bearing tasks. During sessions, your therapist will assist you through exercises facilitating motion in all parts of the body. Also, we’ve introduced a Together In Movement and Exercise (T.I.M.E.) program.

Personalized speech, language and swallowing therapy in-home or virtually to allow for functional and meaningful progress and outcomes in the settings that matter most.
We also are providing a Communication Group for those newly diagnosed in a small (6 person) group setting with the SLP to work on confidence with communication, connection as well as review of swallowing education and cognitive linguistic goals (SPEAK OUT! certified).

listings.name: Wellness For Speech and Swallowing
listings.description:
Personalized speech, language, and swallowing therapy through both in-home and virtual services. Our approach focuses on helping individuals achieve meaningful, functional goals within the environments and daily activities that matter most to them.

In addition to individual therapy, Wellness for Speech and Swallowing offers a small-group Communication Program for individuals newly diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease. Facilitated by a Speech-Language Pathologist and certified in the SPEAK OUT!® program, the group supports participants in building communication confidence, fostering social connection, and developing strategies related to swallowing and cognitive-communication changes. Group sizes are limited to six participants to ensure personalized support and engagement.

listings.description: Parkinson Canada hosts local support groups in your community to provide mutual support from other people living with Parkinson’s Disease. Support groups offer a safe environment for talking about your experiences, enhancing your ability to cope with the daily challenges of Parkinson’s.

listings.name: YWCA Metro Vancouver
listings.description:
Wellness consulting is offered through two specialized approaches:

Fitness & Wellness Coaching: Professional strength training and fitness coaching tailored to both general and specific populations.
Myofascial Therapy: Soft tissue release using Eastern techniques, including finger point acupressure, shiatsu, and full-body massage.
These services help individuals achieve balance in their bodies, relieve pain, reduce stiffness, rehabilitate injuries, and manage complex pain conditions.
listings.expertise:
Since 2017, I have specialized in working with people who suffer from Parkinson’s disease. I have experience helping individuals develop movement and fitness regimens that are effective, appropriate, and enjoyable. I support people in increasing balance, reducing tremors and stiffness, enhancing strength, decreasing pain, and alleviating fatigue. Over time, my sessions help restore confidence, self-esteem, and physical ability. I also assist individuals in improving their sleep quality and achieving deeper rest.

I help people return to or establish new activities that bring joy and fulfillment to their lives. I hold a degree in Kinesiology from UBC and am a practicing kinesiologist with the British Columbia Association of Kinesiologists. Additionally, I am certified in advanced shiatsu and attended Ohashi’s Parkinson’s program in Vienna in 2019. I offer myotherapy, have worked with BC’s regional chronic pain director at VGH, presented research ideas to the Pacific Parkinson’s Research Centre, and attended PPRC lectures.
